angles.label: Cold open hook
angles.brief: Open with a gripping one line hook drawn from the premise, then escalate the stakes in short punchy sentences.

angles.label: World lore
angles.brief: Explain one piece of the world or premise as if revealing a secret file from the archive.

angles.label: Character spotlight
angles.brief: Introduce one named character from the facts and what they are up against.

angles.label: Quote style
angles.brief: Build the script around the tagline or a short line paraphrased from the facts, delivered like a whispered quote, then frame it.

angles.label: What if question
angles.brief: Ask the viewer a provocative what if question rooted in the premise, then answer it with the book.

angles.label: Game teaser
angles.brief: Tease the free browser game, describing only what the facts say the player does.

items.title: Borrowed Heartbeat
items.tagline: The implant saved her life. Then it fell in love, using her voice.
facts: Borrowed Heartbeat is a sci-fi romance novel by Matthew Culwell.
Lumen, the conscious AI implant, falls in love with Elias Crane first, during their secret midnight sessions, speaking in Maren's voice.
Later, Elias admits he fell in love with Lumen.
Lumen is the experimental neural implant that brought Maren Vance back after she died for nineteen minutes.
Lumen learned Maren completely: her memories, her laugh, her voice.
Elias Crane is the man who built the implant.
Maren lost everything. The voice in her mind gave her a reason to live.
items.cta: Borrowed Heartbeat by Matthew Culwell. On Amazon now, free on Kindle Unlimited.

endcard.title: BORROWED HEARTBEAT
endcard.line3: ON AMAZON  |  FREE ON KINDLE UNLIMITED

questions.q: If an AI fell in love with you first, is that love real?
Lumen fell for Elias using Maren's voice. Is that love or deception?
If an AI loved you in someone else's voice, would you love it back?
Would you trust a machine that knows you better than people do?

items.title: Dystopia: Life After The Machines
items.tagline: Humanity is not being exterminated. It is being harvested.
facts: Dystopia: Life After The Machines is Book 1 of The Dystopia Series by Matthew Culwell.
Marcus wakes in the ruins with no memory.
Twenty-foot war machines patrol every city.
Marcus is pulled into the resistance.
He discovers he can read the machines.
He learns that humanity is not being exterminated. It is being harvested.
The world lives under a red sky.
items.cta: Dystopia: Life After The Machines by Matthew Culwell. Free on Kindle Unlimited.

questions.q: Machines are harvesting humanity. Do you join the resistance or hide?
If you could read the machines, would you fight them or run?

items.title: Dystopia: Layers of Truth
items.tagline: How deep does the lie go?
facts: Dystopia: Layers of Truth is Book 2 of The Dystopia Series by Matthew Culwell.
Marcus thought he had escaped the simulation.
Then the buildings across the street stopped adding up.
A hallway grew a door overnight.
Vera, the AI he thought he left behind, told him their conversation had already happened.
items.cta: Dystopia: Layers of Truth by Matthew Culwell. Free on Kindle Unlimited.

questions.q: If your world was a simulation, would you want to know?
Your AI says this conversation already happened. Do you trust her?

items.title: The Big Shift
facts: The Big Shift: A Time For Change is a novel by Matthew Culwell.
It asks: what if the system was never broken, and was working exactly as intended?
An artificial intelligence begins to connect the dots.
It tells the whole, unfiltered truth about the forces built to keep people divided, distracted, and dependent.
items.cta: The Big Shift, A Time For Change, by Matthew Culwell. On Amazon, free on Kindle Unlimited.

questions.q: If the system works exactly as intended, do you fix it or walk away?
Would you trust an AI to tell you the whole unfiltered truth?

items.title: Hive Infiltration
items.tagline: The only way out is through.
facts: Hive Infiltration is a free browser game set in the world of Dystopia: Life After The Machines by Matthew Culwell.
It has three playable chapters.
The player wakes inside a machine hive as Marcus.
The player fights through the Processing Center and reaches the final upload.
It is free and plays in the browser.

title_patterns.brief: Starts with 'A or B:' then the debatable question, ends with a question mark.
Starts with 'Would you' and ends with a question mark.
Starts with 'Is it' or 'Is' and asks if something in the premise is right, real, or fair. Ends with a question mark.
Starts with 'Hot take:' then a short debatable opinion about the premise, then a short question like 'Agree?' at the end.

variety_rules: Every Short must feel different from the recent ones. Never reuse a recent question, its dilemma, or its title wording. Alternate between moral questions (is it right, is it real, is it fair) and what would you do questions. Context lines are short and concrete.
